narr: Upper-level troughing off the west coast promoted a pocket of upper-level divergence over south-central AZ. With MLCAPE values ranging between 250-500 J/kg and PWAT values near 1.5, scattered thunderstorm activity with heavy rainfall rates developed across portions of the Phoenix metro area and were steered northeastward into northern Maricopa County. Although the thunderstorm activity was rather unimpactful, with the flood threat limited due to the fast steering flow, training thunderstorm activity was observed across portions of northern Maricopa County. In particular, an area near Cave Creek experienced flooding impacts during the early morning hours on the 19th with some spots observing upwards of 1.0-1.5 inches. This was enough to cause some of the washes to react, with Sonoran Wash rising above alarm stage.
ev: A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge on Sonoran Wash recorded floodwaters above the pre-determined alarm stage level of 2.0 feet, with the stage peaking at 2.95 feet. The unbridged crossing at North Valley Parkway, approximately 1 mile upstream from the gauge location became impassable. A vehicle was reportedly stuck in the floodwaters requiring the driver to be rescued. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level as well as travel time for the water to reach North Valley Parkway. No injuries reported.
